actual_source_review.public_readout: The fixed-zero dimensionless Hamiltonian, cubic s ramp, logarithmic tilt path, fresh uniform-action and orbital-time preparation, isolated dynamics and ensemble-before-slow-limit total-energy readout are complete and consistent. Paths with equal final Hamiltonians may have different declared initial Hamiltonians.
actual_source_review.source: The starter and completed baseline find the actual path-dependent crossing and preserve outgoing branch actions. Their normalized lobe-area probabilities are a coherent local self-similar allocation closure. All three controls enter the forward model. The oracle changes only those weights to normalized positive lobe growth rates; this is a physical allocation law difference, not an algebraic defect in implementing a stated law.
actual_source_review.domain_and_growth: The independently checked prototype derivation carries through unchanged. The global right-lobe growth bracket is bounded below by .1392709104; left growth is positive. The saddle remains nondegenerate and all allowed preparations start outside and end inside the total separatrix. No shrinking-lobe recrossing or omitted final connected branch occurs in the declared r2 domain.
actual_source_review.calibration: Captured constant-path calibration is exactly shared. The derivative mean(sum alpha_i^2*xi*omega_i) is strictly positive across the unknown interval. Exact slow-limit energy, rather than a finite-ramp surrogate, generates the independent fixed-sigma observations. None constructors, private truth and unrestricted fit API are preserved.
actual_source_review.reference_independence: Initial phase-volume/period preparation is reused from reviewed r1 code. After preparation, the reference propagates q,p and independently accumulates work under the actual two-control path. It reads final Hamiltonian energy without capture probabilities, final branch-action allocation or final-energy inversion. Independence is from the capture prediction, not a claim of unrelated initial geometry code.
actual_source_review.reference_approximation: The fixed reference is a finite-ramp ensemble approximation to the requested slow limit. Every scored input has its own doubled-duration and denser-ensemble comparison; half-step/phase-offset and parameter-edge checks are separate. Nonmonotone finite-grid errors are honestly retained. The measured errors are well below the ordinary .04 gate.
actual_source_review.grader: Four normalized-RMS groups comprise two constant-path anchors and three two-case changing-path groups. Parameter .03, calibration chi-square1.5, prediction .04 and agent600/verifier60 remain unchanged. The ordinary total-energy RMS uses fixed-zero signals, with no background subtraction or artificial near-zero normalization.
actual_source_review.input_isolation: The exact318-byte neutral instruction permits arbitrary implementation replacement. Public Docker copies only README, starter, test and calibration data. No true J0, hint, private solution/reference, AUTHOR or prototype is exposed. Public and private calibration bytes match and all256 rows have the stated fixed sigma.

history.r1_outcomes: Three physical passes, one with a scored agent timeout; six earlier unstarted setup failures remain separate. No prior result is replaced.

qualifications: Zero and arbitrarily small path slopes remain allowed; the models coincide or approach each other there. Discriminating groups have ordinary nonzero slopes, so no uniform discrepancy is claimed over the whole public box.

Finite-ramp calibration discrepancies are larger than the uncertainty of the repeated-data mean and are explicitly separate from exact slow-limit data generation. They are not treated as random measurement noise or used to shift the unknown.

The direct-reference evidence is empirical finite-ensemble convergence at stated settings, not exact infinite-time trajectory certification. Its worst checked scored error .002446 is comfortably below .04.
Local controls certify the harness on this host within60 seconds. They do not certify Docker startup reliability or whether a model will retain the approximation.

A future trajectory that recognizes growth-rate allocation but implements a derivative, normalization or trajectory solver incorrectly must be classified separately from a clean physical-model failure.
This is a genuine path-dependent revision of the existing adiabatic-capture family, not a new unrelated family. All earlier successes and exploratory variants remain preserved.
